designs.name: millbank
designs.prompt: Use case: ui-mockup. Create a high-fidelity desktop web application screenshot, landscape 1536x1024. A practical fictional healthcare simulation interface for a hackathon, with carefully typeset legible UI, believable synthetic content, excellent hierarchy and deliberate spacing. Full-bleed app screenshot, no device frame, no perspective, no presentation decorations. Small 'SIMULATION' label and a quiet 'Neighbourhood' return link. No real vendor logos. Each workplace must have its own information architecture, not a shared patient-banner-and-tabs template. No large left sidebar. Millbank hospital at Northbank General. Hospital operations first: a compact dark navy command header, ward selector 'Acute medicine', shift 'Saturday · 08:00', occupancy summary. Main canvas is a spatial ward/bed board: three clearly labelled bays with four compact patient bed tiles each, bed numbers, fictional patient names, small acuity markers, pending investigations and discharge readiness. A selected bed opens a narrow right clinical handover drawer for 'Amira Khan', with an observation trend, investigations timeline, discharge blockers checklist and 'Open encounter' action. Bottom band is a time-based ward activity strip. Use cool white and slate, restrained cyan and amber, utilitarian sans typography, square dense EPR controls. No giant empty patient banner, no GP journal layout, no serif wordmark, no generic stat-card dashboard. Hospital workflow must be immediately recognisable.

Build around a chronological consultation journal resembling a carefully organised medical desktop application. Narrow top practice bar in muted blue, compact patient search, a slim identity strip for fictional 'Amira Khan · SIM-000001'. Three asymmetrical working regions: today's appointment list in a compact left column (not site navigation), large central consultation journal with dated entries and an inline consultation note editor, narrow right repeat-medication and active-problem lists. Horizontal workflow rail 'Received 8 / Clinical check 3 / Dispensing 4 / Ready 6'. Left quarter is a stacked prescription ticket queue, centre half a selected prescription with medicine line items, dosage labels marked synthetic, stock location, pack quantities and barcode scanning field; right quarter a tall paper dispensing label preview and final checking checklist. Neighbourhood Care community nursing app. A visit planner organised around staff travel and home visits, not a hospital patient table. Light warm canvas, deep teal typography, coral appointment accents. Compact top header with date and team selector. Left third is an illustrated functional street route map with five numbered stops, river and street labels. Each workplace must have its own information architecture, not a shared patient-banner-and-tabs template. No large left sidebar. Eleanor's home personal health dashboard named 'At home'. Consumer wearable dashboard informed by the quiet editorial clarity of Apple Health and Withings but original branding and composition. Airy off-white background, black large humanist type, soft lavender and muted terracotta chart accents. Top 'Good morning, Eleanor' and compact 'Today / Week / Month' segmented control. Asymmetrical editorial grid: large left daily movement ring and short walk timeline; wide centre weekly sleep bars; slim right connected-devices list with a watch and smart scale icon. Lower area a large clean weight trend chart, resting heart rate sparkline and a simple personal care reminder. Clearly marked illustrative synthetic measurements, no diagnostic claims. Comfortable whitespace, restrained soft rounded panels, accessible numbers, no dense clinical toolbar, no patient identifier banner, no sidebar. One discreet 'Share with care team' action.
